description: Chess opening book for GAME channel instant lookup

najdorf.name: Sicilian Najdorf
najdorf.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 d6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nc3 a6
najdorf.evaluation: Equal to slightly better for White
najdorf.key_ideas: Black fights for counterplay on the queenside. The a6 move prevents Bb5 and prepares b5.

dragon.name: Sicilian Dragon
dragon.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 d6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nc3 g6
dragon.key_ideas: Black fianchettoes the bishop on g7 targeting the long diagonal. Yugoslav Attack (Be3, Qd2, 0-0-0) is White's most aggressive response.

classical.name: Sicilian Classical
classical.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 d6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nc3 Nc6
classical.key_ideas: Symmetrical development. White often plays Bg5 (Richter-Rauzer) or Bc4.

morphy_defense.name: Morphy Defense
morphy_defense.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 a6
morphy_defense.key_ideas: a6 asks the bishop its intentions. Leads to deep strategic play.

berlin_defense.name: Berlin Defense
berlin_defense.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 Nf6
berlin_defense.key_ideas: The Berlin Wall endgame after 4. 0-0 Nxe4 5. d4 is a famous defense used by Kramnik to dethrone Kasparov.

declined.name: Queen's Gambit Declined
declined.key_ideas: Black maintains the d5 pawn. Leads to classical positional play.

accepted.name: Queen's Gambit Accepted
accepted.key_ideas: Black gives up center temporarily for activity. White recaptures easily.

slav.name: Slav Defense
slav.key_ideas: Black supports d5 with c6, keeping the light-squared bishop active.

evans_gambit.name: Evans Gambit
evans_gambit.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5 4. b4
evans_gambit.evaluation: Sharp gambit, good for White in practice
evans_gambit.key_ideas: White sacrifices a pawn for rapid development and central control.

two_knights.name: Two Knights Defense
two_knights.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Nf6
two_knights.key_ideas: Black counterattacks immediately. After 4. Ng5, the Fried Liver Attack (5. Nxf7) is a famous trap.

winawer.name: Winawer Variation
winawer.moves: 1. e4 e6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3 Bb4
winawer.key_ideas: Black pins the knight and creates pawn structure tension.

advance.name: Advance Variation
advance.evaluation: Space for White, counterplay for Black
advance.key_ideas: White gains space. Black undermines with c5 and plans f6 break.

advance.name: Advance Variation
advance.evaluation: Space advantage for White, solid for Black
advance.key_ideas: White gains space. Black undermines with c5 and plans to break open the position.

classical.name: Classical Variation
classical.moves: 1. e4 c6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3 dxe4 4. Nxe4 Bf5
classical.key_ideas: Black develops the light-squared bishop outside the pawn chain before playing e6.

classical.name: Classical Variation
classical.evaluation: Strategic battle, both sides have chances
classical.key_ideas: Black plays for a kingside attack with f5, White expands on the queenside with c5.

samisch.name: Samisch Variation
samisch.evaluation: White aims for a strong center
samisch.key_ideas: f3 supports e4 and prepares Be3. White often castles queenside for an attacking game.

symmetrical.name: Symmetrical English
symmetrical.key_ideas: Mirror structure leads to Maroczy Bind or Hedgehog formations.
